shortcuts.navigation.title: Navigation: “g” then a letter
shortcuts.note: Pages without a letter are still reachable through the palette, which lists every page of the application.
aide.shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
aide.shortcuts.summary: Move from one screen to another and find a staff member without leaving the keyboard.
aide.shortcuts.intro: Ctrl+K opens the command palette: a single field that leads to any page of the application and also searches the reference data — a staff member (their timeline opens), a stand or a time slot (the calendar opens on it). The arrow keys walk the list, Enter opens, Esc closes. This is the one to remember: every other shortcut is only a shorthand for something the palette already does.
aide.shortcuts.def.palette: Opens (and closes) the command palette. The browser does not receive this shortcut while a tab of the application is in the foreground.
aide.shortcuts.def.help: Shows the full list of shortcuts, without leaving the current screen.
aide.shortcuts.def.filter: Puts the caret in the filter of the current page, when it has one (the reference-data pages, and this help page).
aide.shortcuts.def.submit: Submits the form being filled in, like a click on its save button. A form whose button is disabled (an incomplete entry) is not saved for all that: the keyboard does nothing the mouse is refused.
aide.shortcuts.def.escape: Closes the open window (palette, form, confirmation) and gives the focus back to wherever it was opened from.
aide.shortcuts.go: To jump straight to a screen, type “g” then the letter of the destination — “g” then “a” for the staff members. Pages with no letter remain reachable through the palette, which lists them all.
aide.shortcuts.tables: The reference-data tables (staff, stands, time slots, locations, game categories) are keyboard-navigable too. The shortest way in: “/” puts the cursor in the page filter, type enough to narrow the list, then Arrow down jumps straight onto the first row. Tab enters them too, on a single row — never row by row — but it first walks through the header controls (the “select all” checkbox and every sortable header). The arrow keys then move the focus one step at a time; Tab leaves the row towards its buttons, then towards the rest of the page.
aide.shortcuts.def.rowEnter: Enters the table without counting tab stops: the focus jumps onto the current row, the one an outline marks. This is the gesture to remember — filter, then go down. Clicking a row focuses it the same way, and the arrow keys carry on from there.
aide.shortcuts.def.rowMove: Move from one row to the next. Home and End jump to the first and the last displayed row. The focus follows the row, not its rank: changing the sort does not send it elsewhere, and filtering the focused row out leaves it on whichever row takes its place.
aide.shortcuts.def.rowOpen: Opens the focused row: its detail view, or straight away its form on the time slots, which have no detail view. Like the row's own buttons, the key stays inert for as long as a solve locks the edition.
aide.shortcuts.def.rowSelect: Ticks or unticks the focused row. The bulk actions bar appears with the first ticked row, exactly as with the mouse.
aide.shortcuts.guard: No single-key shortcut fires while you are typing text: as long as the caret is in a field, “g”, “/” and “?” stay ordinary characters. They come back as soon as the focus leaves the field.
importCsv.intro: Drop the spreadsheet of your volunteers, exported as CSV, say which column is which field, read what the import would do, then confirm. Nothing is written before that confirmation: until you click « Import », this screen only reads your file. The file stays in memory and is never saved on the server.
importCsv.fichier.aide: CSV only — comma, semicolon or tab separator, recognised on its own. An .xlsx workbook must first be saved again as CSV from your spreadsheet application.
importCsv.fichier.format: The birth date is required to create a fiche: the whole minor / adult regime derives from it. Competences, wishes and off days may hold several values in one cell, separated by « | ». A competence is written « category » or « category:REFERENT ».
importCsv.fichier.aideDetaillee: Every detail in the help page
importCsv.mapping.aide: A mapping is proposed from the headers; correct it freely. A field left on « — » is not in the file: it will not touch the fiches already stored.
importCsv.options.remplacerAnimateurs: Full replacement: delete the animateurs the file does not name
importCsv.options.remplacerAnimateursAid: Unticked (the default), the import adds and updates, and never deletes anybody. Ticked, it refuses to run while a row is rejected — it would otherwise delete the very people those rows failed to describe.
importCsv.options.remplacementBloque: A full replacement cannot run while a row is rejected: fix the file, or untick this box to import without deleting anybody.
importCsv.options.remplacerJours: Replace the off days instead of adding to them
importCsv.options.remplacerJoursAide: Unticked (the default), the file's days are added to the ones already stored: a catch-up import does not erase what the animateurs declared themselves.
importCsv.rapport.sousTitreApplique: Imported in a single transaction: these figures are the database's.
importCsv.rapport.sousTitrePreview: Nothing was written. Nothing reaches the database until you click « Import ».
importCsv.rapport.vide: The file carries no data row under its header.
importCsv.confirmer.ajout: Import {$acceptees} row(s)? The animateurs the file does not name are kept.
importCsv.confirmer.remplacement: Import {$acceptees} row(s) and delete {$supprimes} animateur(s) the file does not name?
